children: Shares of DXC Technology slipped after the company cut its revenue and adjusted earnings forecast for the current fiscal year and reported lower revenue and earnings for the second quarter.
The stock tumbled 13%, to $13.25, after ending the session down 5.3%. Shares hit a 52-week high of $16.38 on Monday and are up 4% this year.

DXC lowered its revenue outlook for fiscal 2027 to $11.91 billion to $11.98 billion, which it said would be a decline of 5% to 5.5% from the previous from year. The company had previously guided for revenue of $12.1 billion to $12.35 billion.
Analysts are expecting revenue of $12.14 billion, according to a FactSet survey.
Stripping out one-time items, DXC expects earnings of $2.25 to $2.50 a share, down from the $2.40 to $2.90 expected in July. Wall Street has forecasted adjusted earnings of $2.58 per share.
For the second quarter, net income came in at $24 million, or 15 cents a share, down from $36 million and 20 cents a share a year ago.
Adjusted earnings were 67 cents a share, topping the 55-cent estimate of both FactSet and the company.
Revenue totaled $3.03 billion, down from the $3.16 billion reported in the same period a year ago, but ahead of the $2.98 billion expected by analysts.
The provider of technology consulting, outsourcing and support services added that discussions are continuing regarding a possible sale of its insurance business.
